payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When the directory argument is a repository root that holds .basicly/ledger, the kit reads and writes that ledger
- When the directory argument is omitted, the kit uses .basicly/ledger under the current directory
- When a read names a directory that holds no ledger, the kit exits non-zero with a message and writes nothing
- init creates .basicly/ledger
- A regression test runs the documented create . and list . forms
payload.description: When a consumer runs the documented command cli.py create . on a fresh init, the kit writes pending-main.jsonl into the repository root and init never creates .basicly/ledger, so the post-merge hook folds a different directory. cli.py list . in this repository returns count 0 while cli.py list .basicly/ledger returns 1398, and the read writes snapshot.jsonl into the root.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- The owner decides between: keep the writer class only, record an opt-in shared identity such as git user.email, or drop the field and rely on git history
- The chosen form is written by the engine and the standalone kit alike
payload.description: When several developers share one ledger, I want each event to say who wrote it, so I can answer who changed a record. Measured 2026-09-23 over all 9842 events: 3775 <redacted:machine-username> (imported rows), 3235 operator:<redacted:machine-username>, 2642 empty, 177 unattributed:no-actor-supplied, 13 agent:claude. owned_write.resolved_actor builds the operator value from getpass.getuser() and then redacts that same name, so it is the same constant for every human on every machine; no configuration changes it. The standalone kit CLI passes no actor, so every standalone write is unattributed. Readers: fsck counts unattributed events, provenance prints by <actor>, tracker export scrubs it; no gate or decision reads it.
payload.requirements: - No machine username, path or hostname in a tracked file (portability rule)
payload.title: The event actor names a class of writer and never a person

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: Decided (owner delegated the judgement): the actor records the writer class, not a person. Kit writers.py: BR_AGENT_NAME, else AI_AGENT, else CLAUDECODE=1 -> agent:<name>, else operator; name limited to [A-Za-z0-9._-] and 64 chars. Kit commands and engine owned_write both use it. The person is the git author of the commit carrying the line; an email in the ledger would duplicate git and risk internal-info-scan. Tests: 7 marker cases, sanitising, cap, standalone CLI write, engine seam writes (markers cleared, since this session sets AI_AGENT and CLAUDECODE). By hand: session writes agent:claude-code_2-1-280_agent, env -u markers writes operator. uv run pytest -q: 6014 passed 1 xfailed.

payload.acceptance_criteria: derive_phase does not return ship unless the verify precondition holds (verified) in addition to the ship checkpoint being approved; a ship-approved node whose verify gate is not green and whose worktree is bound derives as build so the next advance re-runs the landing; a regression case is added to the existing test_derive_phase_ladder parametrization; the full test suite including the feature/epic ship path in test_loop and test_cli_loop stays green
payload.description:
derive_phase (loop_state.py) returns the ship phase the moment 'ship' is in the approved checkpoints, ignoring whether the verify gate passed and the worktree branch merged. So approving the ship checkpoint on an un-landed node (e.g. after a build->verify landing failed on a transient .git/index.lock, or any premature approval) wedges the phase at ship: _on_ship correctly refuses to close an unmerged branch, but br has no comment-delete and there is no supported un-approve, so the phase cannot fall back to build to re-run the landing. Recovery today requires manual ff-merge plus basicly verify --issue from base. Fix: require the verify precondition on the ship rung so a premature ship approval no longer changes the phase and the landing re-runs on the next advance (self-healing). Incident during basicly-j9w4.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Provision a leaf's build worktree through the loop and commit its work on the harness branch.
2. Run `basicly loop advance <id>` for the build->verify landing but have it fail before merging (e.g. a transient `.git/index.lock` makes pre-commit `git write-tree` fail, so the verify gate is not recorded and the branch is not merged).
3. Approve the ship checkpoint anyway: `basicly policy checkpoint <id> ship --approve --confirm <code>`.
4. Run `basicly loop advance <id>`.

Expected: the landing re-runs, because the branch is unmerged and verify is unrecorded.
Actual: derive_phase reports phase=ship (ship is in the approved checkpoints), `_on_ship` refuses to close the unmerged branch, and there is no supported way back to the landing, so the track is wedged.
payload.title: Loop wedges when ship is approved before the verify landing lands

## Trigger

payload.description:
## Context

Owner directive 2026-08-22, after reading the live wall while four lanes were building: *"We need improvements all over the board. I give you the autonomy to iterate and build an enterprise professional board that is informative to humans so that agents can work unattended and we always know what is going on and on what thing are agents working."*

Seven complaints were named. Each was traced to code and filed as its own record. This record exists because nine independent patches on the present layout would not add up to the board the directive asks for. It is the design those nine build toward, and it is approved.

## The question the board must answer

**What is happening right now, and does it need me?**

Everything on the page earns its space against that question. A reader arriving cold must learn, without a second source: whether the factory is running, what each agent is working on this second, whether anything is stuck, and what a stuck thing needs from them.

## The principles

**The reader is an operator, never a producer author.** No word on the page may name a role the reader does not hold. `producer`, `emitted`, `section`, `withheld` and `renderable` are engine vocabulary and do not appear. A diagnostic a producer author needs is reachable, and it is not a standing row.

**A state is worth one channel, not three.** The present design gives every state a glyph, a border style and a colour for the same fact, and says so at `board_wall.py:14-15`. Colour plus a word replaces all three.

**A quantity is stated once, in one unit.** The present band states one wait as `6 DAYS` and as `160h 16m`.

**Colour means severity, not existence.** The page's alarm channel fires today whenever an ask exists. A five second wait and a six day wait must not paint the same.

**Space is spent on what is uncertain.** A green state is a word. An exception expands. This continues the principle `basicly-7ogfbq` landed rather than replacing it.

**Every figure names its own denomination.** A live token estimate and a recorded token figure are different quantities. Where both exist, both are shown and each is named.

## The layout, top to bottom

**1. Status line.** Repo, branch, head, the gate verdict as `GATES n/n`, and how fresh the document is. One line, recessive.

**2. The alarm, only when there is one.** Its severity comes from the wait duration against declared thresholds. It states in plain words what has stopped, that a person is what stops it, how long, and the command that answers it. Absent when nothing waits.

**3. RUNNING NOW - the hero region.** One card per adopted lane, carrying: the unit id, the feature it serves, its phase, the agent and model running it, how long it has run, what it has spent, and **the last thing it said**. That last field is what tells a working lane from a wedged one, and no other field can.

**4. The grant.** One bar: live spend against the budget, with the live figure named as an estimate that reads high, and the recorded figure named as the one that lands at completion.

**5. NEXT UP, grouped by the feature each row serves.** A heading per epic with its ready count, rows beneath. Units attached to no feature form their own group with a count, because that count is itself a finding - 45 of 190 today. Depth is spent on the highest-priority features and the row budget is computed from the viewport, not fixed.

**6. Footer.** Backlog totals, agent health, lifetime spend. No producer diagnostics.

## What was built and measured

A working mockup was generated from the live `/snapshot.json` and the supervisor's own terminal line, and every figure in it is real. It renders clean at 1200, 1440 and 1920 - `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` reports neither overflow nor overlap at any of the three.

Two fields in it come from the supervisor's terminal rather than the document, and that is exactly what `basicly-0hxck3` fixes. The grant bar reads 20.7% where the live board reads 0%, and that is `basicly-wctp0g`.

## The children

- `basicly-0hxck3` the lane card, which is the hero region's producer
- `basicly-eaw1dy` the feature name on a row
- `basicly-v8jwf0` the alarm band's severity and wording
- `basicly-jbd80w` the producer diagnostics leaving the human surface
- `basicly-ffm2yp` the row budget computed from the viewport
- `basicly-a68ggd` the loop region showing the pass rather than the backlog
- `basicly-wctp0g` the spend meter that can move while a lane runs

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN every child has landed, A READER ARRIVING COLD SHALL be able to say what each agent is working on and whether anything needs them, from the page alone.
- WHEN the page renders, IT SHALL contain none of the words `producer`, `emitted`, `withheld` or `renderable`.
- WHEN a figure is shown, ITS DENOMINATION SHALL be stated where two denominations exist.
- WHEN the page renders at every width the layout claims, `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` SHALL report neither overflow nor overlap.
- WHERE a child would satisfy its own criteria while contradicting this design, THIS DESIGN SHALL win and the child SHALL be re-scoped rather than landed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`

payload.text:
[pre-merge verification 2026-08-22] All six unlanded branches were merged in landing order into a scratch tree and the result was rendered and looked at, before the supervisor attempted it.

MERGE: rn0o.6, fi1i7z, eaw1dy, 0hxck3, kn4rip and 6oa3mt produce exactly ONE conflict across the whole chain - docs/plan/implementation-plan.md on eaw1dy - and that file is already declared regenerable in preflight's regen line, rebuilt by docs_claims.py --fix --block plan-current-state, spending no rework. Zero conflicts land on a file the engine cannot rebuild. Individually all six also merge clean onto main; the cumulative order is what surfaced the one.

RENDER: the wall groups by feature. Five headings drew, each with its ready count - the board epic 2, vkh0 18, u6jq 3, u2hl 22, and 'Not attached to any feature' 31. That last count is the finding the flat wall hid: 31 ready records serve no feature and cannot be dispatched by supervise over an epic.

GEOMETRY: check_render_overflow reports neither overflow nor overlap at 1200, 1440 and 1920, and the instrument was shown to fire on both shipped fixtures first, so the three greens are evidence rather than a broken probe.

STILL OPEN ON THE STATIC PATH, and it is a68ggd rather than a regression: board --out hard-codes in_flight False, so RUN, GATES, SPEND and the lane cards render as absent even while a supervisor ticks. Under a live supervisor they populate. The alarm band and the section chip row are untouched, being v8jwf0 and jbd80w.

The merged tree was b8638c19; the scratch worktree is removed.

[fable-5 design of record 2026-08-22] Two Fable 5 architects reviewed the live page at 1280, 1600 and 1920 and returned a design. Recorded here because nine child records were each about to invent their own answer.

TWO DISCOVERIES THAT CHANGE THE ORDER OF WORK.

First: every id on the page already joins to a human title on the snapshot. lanes[].id and asks[].issue join to units[].title, verified resolving for both live lanes and the live ask. The owner's complaint that internal ids mean nothing is a JOIN THAT COSTS NOTHING, not a producer change - units is already on every snapshot this producer emits.

Second: the truncation and the dead area are ONE CSS decision, not two defects. A fixed 470px right column at board_page.html.j2:59 plus a minmax(0,1fr) stretch row at :72 leaves about 70 percent of a 1920x2400 render black WHILE clipping claude-opu... even at 1920. Kill the fixed layout first and every later item gets its width for free.

THE STATE-MARKER RULING, argued rather than asserted. Delete the glyph channel entirely - all eight STATES glyphs at board_wall.py:67-76, here_glyph and none_glyph at board_render.py:83-84, and every .glyph and .chip in the template. board_wall.py:14-15's own docstring proves the glyph is the redundant third channel, and it is the FAILING channel: the mono stack at template :24-25 guarantees no coverage for U+25CF, which is the owner's tofu. The three-channel rule survives as WORD plus COLOUR plus BORDER. A word never tofus, survives a monochrome projector, and names the state to a colour-blind reader better than a diamond does.

  renders  -> no mark. It is the default state of everything; marking it is pure noise.
  live     -> no mark. Presence under RUNNING NOW asserts it. Mark the exception: live false prints 'not confirmed live'.
  absent   -> words, dim, footer only, once in a roster sentence. An owner can do nothing about an absence.
  withheld -> amber left border plus the word WITHHELD plus the violation, in place. Data existed and failed the contract; that is a defect someone fixes.
  alarm    -> colour fill plus an all-caps word plus top position. The two real alarms get all three surviving channels.

THE CARD. Three lines, full page width, and 'not measured' is NEVER printed. Line one is the phase plus 'started N ago' from lanes[].started_at - the label says started, never 'running for', so it cannot be misread as dispatch time. Line two is the unit TITLE via the join. Line three is id, agent, model, branch in dim mono, about 590px at 13px against a 1248px box, so the model id is readable at 1280 with 2x headroom. A metrics line appears ONLY when at least one of tokens, cost, context or rework is present. The correct absences the producer protects therefore render as nothing rather than as six labelled apologies, and the footer roster stays the auditable inventory.

THE ACTION BAND, exact copy for the live ask:

  NEEDS YOU - approve the "ship" checkpoint on basicly-b2n2                6 DAYS
  A stale database auto-flush silently deletes committed records
  waiting since Fri 15 Aug 16:59 UTC - this unit is stopped at ship until you approve
  > basicly policy checkpoint basicly-b2n2 ship --approve

The verb derives from asks[].kind. The duration is stated ONCE in the headline and the second spelling becomes an absolute date, so it answers 'since when' rather than repeating the elapsed. Orange fill only at or above one hour: cadence is 15s and a checkpoint answered within the hour is normal attended turnaround, so orange must mean you have been the bottleneck for a while or the one signal the page exists for trains the owner to ignore it.

NEXT UP. Title first and dominant, type as a one-word dim prefix, id LAST and dim - kept because every command takes an id, demoted from label to address. Feature grouping stays exactly as landed including the unattached group sorting last with its true count, because that heading is itself a finding.

RANKED BUILD ORDER: 1 kill the fixed layout, 2 the lane card, 3 the action band, 4 delete the glyph channel, 5 the next-up row order, 6 th

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When an operator watches many agents work unattended, I want the board to state what each agent does and whether it needs the operator, so I can run the factory from the page alone.

## Context

Owner directive 2026-08-22, after reading the live wall while four lanes were building: *"We need improvements all over the board. I give you the autonomy to iterate and build an enterprise professional board that is informative to humans so that agents can work unattended and we always know what is going on and on what thing are agents working."*

Seven complaints were named. Each was traced to code and filed as its own record. This record exists because nine independent patches on the present layout would not add up to the board the directive asks for. It is the design those nine build toward, and it is approved.

## The question the board must answer

**What is happening right now, and does it need me?**

Everything on the page earns its space against that question. A reader arriving cold must learn, without a second source: whether the factory is running, what each agent is working on this second, whether anything is stuck, and what a stuck thing needs from them.

## The principles

**The reader is an operator, never a producer author.** No word on the page may name a role the reader does not hold. `producer`, `emitted`, `section`, `withheld` and `renderable` are engine vocabulary and do not appear. A diagnostic a producer author needs is reachable, and it is not a standing row.

**A state is worth one channel, not three.** The present design gives every state a glyph, a border style and a colour for the same fact, and says so at `board_wall.py:14-15`. Colour plus a word replaces all three.

**A quantity is stated once, in one unit.** The present band states one wait as `6 DAYS` and as `160h 16m`.

**Colour means severity, not existence.** The page's alarm channel fires today whenever an ask exists. A five second wait and a six day wait must not paint the same.

**Space is spent on what is uncertain.** A green state is a word. An exception expands. This continues the principle `basicly-7ogfbq` landed rather than replacing it.

**Every figure names its own denomination.** A live token estimate and a recorded token figure are different quantities. Where both exist, both are shown and each is named.

## The layout, top to bottom

**1. Status line.** Repo, branch, head, the gate verdict as `GATES n/n`, and how fresh the document is. One line, recessive.

**2. The alarm, only when there is one.** Its severity comes from the wait duration against declared thresholds. It states in plain words what has stopped, that a person is what stops it, how long, and the command that answers it. Absent when nothing waits.

**3. RUNNING NOW - the hero region.** One card per adopted lane, carrying: the unit id, the feature it serves, its phase, the agent and model running it, how long it has run, what it has spent, and **the last thing it said**. That last field is what tells a working lane from a wedged one, and no other field can.

**4. The grant.** One bar: live spend against the budget, with the live figure named as an estimate that reads high, and the recorded figure named as the one that lands at completion.

**5. NEXT UP, grouped by the feature each row serves.** A heading per epic with its ready count, rows beneath. Units attached to no feature form their own group with a count, because that count is itself a finding - 45 of 190 today. Depth is spent on the highest-priority features and the row budget is computed from the viewport, not fixed.

**6. Footer.** Backlog totals, agent health, lifetime spend. No producer diagnostics.

## What was built and measured

A working mockup was generated from the live `/snapshot.json` and the supervisor's own terminal line, and every figure in it is real. It renders clean at 1200, 1440 and 1920 - `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` reports neither overflow nor overlap at any of the three.

Two fields in it come from the supervisor's terminal rather than the document, and that is exactly what `basicly-0hxck3` fixes. The grant bar reads 20.7% where the live board reads 0%, and that is `basicly-wctp0g`.

## The children

- `basicly-0hxck3` the lane card, which is the hero region's producer
- `basicly-eaw1dy` the feature name on a row
- `basicly-v8jwf0` the alarm band's severity and wording
- `basicly-jbd80w` the producer diagnostics leaving the human surface
- `basicly-ffm2yp` the row budget computed from the viewport
- `basicly-a68ggd` the loop region showing the pass rather than the backlog
- `basicly-wctp0g` the spend meter that can move while a lane runs

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`

The page shall use word plus colour plus border to mark a state, never a redundant third channel, and shall state each figure's denomination where two exist. The page shall render with no overflow and no overlap at 1200, 1440 and 1920 pixels wide.

payload.description:
## Context

Found by the security reviewer the engine dispatched at VALIDATE on `basicly-62h3x9`, 2026-09-06, with a probe it ran rather than an argument it made. The code is on main.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pick an output directory a second party can write to, which `basicly board --out` creates itself.
2. Plant a symlink at `record/<any-id-in-units>.html` pointing at a file the board's user can write.
3. Run `basicly board --out <that directory>/board.html`.

Observed, from the reviewer's probe:

```
written,refused: (1, 0)
target head: <!doctype html>|<html lang="en">|  <head
```

The target file lost its content. Expected: the write refuses a path that is a symlink and reports it as refused.

## What is and is not being claimed

**Not path traversal.** `board_record.SAFE_ID` is anchored at both ends and holds; the path stays inside `record/`. `board_serve`'s `<redacted:posix-absolute-path><id>` route reaches no filesystem at all - it is a dict lookup - and `board.record("../../etc/passwd", ...)` returns `None`.

**What changed with `basicly-62h3x9`.** The class is pre-existing for the two files `board --out` already wrote. That record made the names **predictable and numerous** - one per record in `units`, 297 today - and made the tool create the directory itself. An attacker plants rather than guesses.

**Exposure is low and stated as low.** The reviewer's own words: *"high that the write follows the link, low that anybody runs the board with a shared output directory outside the demonstration line."* This is filed because the fix is small and the finding is demonstrated, not because the risk is pressing.

## Also unverified, deliberately left as a note

A Windows device name - `CON`, `NUL`, `COM1` - passes `SAFE_ID` and would become `record/CON.html`. The reviewer was on Linux and could not run it, so it is stated as unverified rather than filed as a finding. Settle it on Windows before treating it as either.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a page's destination path exists and is a symbolic link, THE WRITER SHALL refuse that page and count it among the refused, rather than following the link.
- THE COMMAND SHALL report the refusal count it already prints, so a refused page is visible to the operator rather than silent.
- WHERE a destination is refused, THE OTHER PAGES SHALL still be written: one hostile entry must not cost the whole render.
- A TEST SHALL plant a symlink at a destination, run the writer, and assert the link target is unchanged - the shape the reviewer's own probe took.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `tests/test_board_cli.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.security.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `tests/test_board_cli.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: plant a symlink at one record's destination, run `basicly board --out`, and read the unchanged target beside a refusal count of one.

payload.description:
## Context

Found in the blind read of the board minutes after `basicly-kqh9dj8` merged, which is the change that introduced it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Land a lane so its branch merges into main, leaving the worktree standing until ship tears it down.
2. `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>` and read its card.

Observed, 2026-09-06, on two cards at once:

```
a developer opens one record on the board ...   QUEUED - VERIFY
  id basicly-62h3x9      a worktree with no commits and no changes
work in a live worktree is invisible ...        QUEUED - VERIFY
  id basicly-kqh9dj8     a worktree with no commits and no changes
```

Both had merged. Their code was on main as the card was drawn.

Expected: a card that says the work landed and the worktree is waiting to be torn down.

## Cause

`board_unsupervised.state_for` reads `ahead` - commits the branch holds that base does not - and treats `0` as "nothing here". `0` is the answer for **two** different lanes: one that merged, whose commits are now in base, and one that has not started. The producer's own docstring says so and calls them the same thing: *"A merged branch answers 0, as does one that did nothing; neither is work in flight."*

That reasoning is right about *work in flight* and wrong about what to draw. Neither is in flight, but only one of them is finished, and `queued` is the wrong word for finished.

## The vocabulary question this raises

`board_sections.LANE_STATES` is `queued running waits-to-land landing refused parked`. None of the six means "merged, waiting for teardown". So this is either a seventh state, or a `state_detail` that carries the distinction under `queued`.

Prefer the detail unless a reader needs to filter on it: the closed set is a schema enum that `basicly-ncday7` established, and widening it is a contract change every consumer must follow. The phase already carries the truth beside the state - both cards read `VERIFY`, which is past build - so the pair is not ambiguous to a reader who knows the loop. It is ambiguous to everyone else, which is who the board is for.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane's branch holds no commits base lacks AND its phase is past build, THE CARD SHALL say the work merged and the worktree awaits teardown, not that the worktree has no commits.
- WHERE a lane's branch holds no commits and its phase is at or before build, THE PRESENT wording SHALL be unchanged: that worktree really has done nothing yet.
- A TEST SHALL drive both cases through one function and assert the two produce different text, because one integer answers for both and only the phase separates them.

## Context

Found in the blind read of the board minutes after `basicly-kqh9dj8` merged, which is the change that introduced it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Land a lane so its branch merges into main, leaving the worktree standing until ship tears it down.
2. `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>` and read its card.

Observed, 2026-09-06, on two cards at once:

```
a developer opens one record on the board ...   QUEUED - VERIFY
  id basicly-62h3x9      a worktree with no commits and no changes
work in a live worktree is invisible ...        QUEUED - VERIFY
  id basicly-kqh9dj8     a worktree with no commits and no changes
```

Both had merged. Their code was on main as the card was drawn.

Expected: a card that says the work landed and the worktree is waiting to be torn down.

## Cause

`board_unsupervised.state_for` reads `ahead` - commits the branch holds that base does not - and treats `0` as "nothing here". `0` is the answer for **two** different lanes: one that merged, whose commits are now in base, and one that has not started. The producer's own docstring says so and calls them the same thing: *"A merged branch answers 0, as does one that did nothing; neither is work in flight."*

That reasoning is right about *work in flight* and wrong about what to draw. Neither is in flight, but only one of them is finished, and `queued` is the wrong word for finished.

## The vocabulary question this raises

`board_sections.LANE_STATES` is `queued running waits-to-land landing refused parked`. None of the six means "merged, waiting for teardown". So this is either a seventh state, or a `state_detail` that carries the distinction under `queued`.

Prefer the detail unless a reader needs to filter on it: the closed set is a schema enum that `basicly-ncday7` established, and widening it is a contract change every consumer must follow. The phase already carries the truth beside the state - both cards read `VERIFY`, which is past build - so the pair is not ambiguous to a reader who knows the loop. It is ambiguous to everyone else, which is who the board is for.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane's branch holds no commits base lacks AND its phase is past build, THE CARD SHALL say the work merged and the worktree awaits teardown, not that the worktree has no commits.
- WHERE a lane's branch holds no commits and its phase is at or before build, THE PRESENT wording SHALL be unchanged: that worktree really has done nothing yet.
- A TEST SHALL drive both cases through one function and assert the two produce different text, because one integer answers for both and only the phase separates them.

## The vocabulary question, decided against what this record first proposed

This record argued for carrying the distinction in `state_detail` under `queued`, to avoid
widening a closed schema enum. **The rendered board refuted that.** The owner read a wall
where three of five cards led with `QUEUED` in caps and colour and asked what was going on;
the detail sat in small text underneath and did not reach them. The badge is the reader's
channel, so `landed` is a seventh state rather than a footnote on the sixth.

Widening it costs four spellings that have to move together, and the repo already has the
gate that says so: `test_the_closed_state_set_is_spelled_the_same_in_all_three_places`
refused the change until the constant, the bounded set and the schema enum all carried it,
and `test_each_pass_state_leads_the_headline_with_its_own_word_and_no_glyph` refused it until
the consumer had a word and a colour for it.

## Context

Third instance of one root cause, found 2026-09-06 by watching the header go blank the moment a supervisor exited cleanly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Work a repository with `basicly loop run` only, so no supervisor lock is ever taken.
2. `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>` and read the header's run line.

Observed:

```
RUN not emitted by this producer
NOT DRAWN  session - not in this snapshot
```

Expected: the run's record, its grant level, its token budget and its spend, which are facts about the repository and not about a process.

## Cause, and why it is a pattern

`board_serve.session_facts` returns None unless `supervise.read_holder` finds a lock file. `board_facts.session_facts` adds the grant on top and inherits the same gate. So the run line, the grant level, the budget bar and the spend figure all exist only while a supervisor process holds a lock.

This is the **third** capability keyed on that lock rather than on the work:

| capability | record | state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lane rows in `RUNNING NOW` | `basicly-kqh9dj8` | fixed 2026-09-06 |
| the six lane states `LANE_STATES` ships | `basicly-ncday7` | shipped, then unreachable, reached by the fix above |
| the run line: record, grant, budget, spend | **this record** | open |

Each was built for the supervised pass and each is absent on the single-lane path, and in every case the absence rendered as an absence of *work* rather than an absence of *a supervisor*.

## Why nobody noticed until now

A stale lock kept it alive. `read_holder` returns the holder whatever its age and the caller marks it `stale = age_s > STALE_AFTER_S`, so a lock left by a dead session still fed the header - the board drew `RUN basicly-k6tpep - open - L3 - 103%` all day with no supervisor anywhere. A detached `loop supervise` run then took that lock and released it cleanly on exit, which removed it, and the header went blank.

So the header was not working; it was being fed by a corpse. That is worse than it having been blank all along, because the figure it drew - a grant bar at 103% - was the only warning anywhere that the session had gone human-only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a repository has an active grant and no supervisor holds a lock, THE HEADER SHALL still name the granted root, its level, its budget and its spend.
- WHERE a supervisor does hold a lock, THE PRESENT behaviour SHALL be unchanged, including the stale marking.
- WHERE the run line is derived without a lock, IT SHALL NOT claim a pass is running: the grant is a fact about the repository and the pass is a fact about a process, and the header must not merge them.
- A TEST SHALL build the header with no lock present and assert the grant figures are drawn, with a control asserting no pass is claimed.
- THE THREE CAPABILITIES ABOVE SHALL share one test naming every board fact that is allowed to depend on the lock, so a fourth cannot be added silently.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_serve.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: with no supervisor and no lock file, render the board and read the granted root, its level, its budget and its spend on the header.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06: *"board shows 2 cards in parked - build, which is an indicator to me that nothing is happening and everything is waiting, contrary to the 'nothing is waiting' large text on the board."*

Both readings were the board's fault. The banner said `NOTHING IS WAITING` and the region beneath it said `waits for the next pass - 2 lane(s) parked`, so the page contradicted itself in the two largest type sizes it has.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Leave two worktrees on disk whose records are `parked` - one deferred, one abandoned - and no lane running.
2. `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>` and read the line under `RUNNING NOW`.

Observed: `waits for the next pass - 2 lane(s) parked`.

Expected: no pass exists to wait for, so the region says what a reader can act on.

## Cause

`board_regions._waiting_on` is a ladder, and its third rung fired on any state in `LANE_MARKS`:

```python
stopped = [state for state in held if state in LANE_MARKS]
if stopped:
    return f"waits for the next pass - {len(stopped)} lane(s) {words}"
```

`parked` is in `LANE_MARKS`, so two dead worktrees produced a sentence promising a pass that was never coming. `basicly-3iaw0x` is deferred by owner decision of 2026-09-01 and `basicly-fiow1sr` is an abandoned worktree held on purpose; no pass will adopt either.

`landed` had the same problem the moment it was added (`basicly-k6tpep.4`): finished work would have read as waiting too.

The rung's own docstring already states the rule it broke - *"A rung must not answer a question it cannot"* - written when the blocked count fired on an idle factory (`basicly-9guj21`). This is the same defect one rung higher.

## Fix

`LANE_RESUMABLE = {queued, waits-to-land, refused}` - the stopped states a pass will come back to. `parked` and `landed` are excluded, and the fall-through guard reads the same set, so a board holding nothing but parked and landed worktrees drops to the ready count instead of describing a pass that does not exist.

Measured after: `no pass is running - 239 record(s) are ready to start`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE every lane is `parked` or `landed`, THE REGION SHALL NOT say the pass waits for them, and SHALL fall through to what a reader can start.
- WHERE a lane is `queued`, `waits-to-land` or `refused`, THE PRESENT sentence SHALL be unchanged: a pass really will come back to those.
- THE BANNER AND THE REGION SHALL NOT disagree: when the banner says nothing is waiting, no line beneath it may say something is.
- A TEST SHALL drive a board whose only lanes are parked and assert the ready count is reported, with a control asserting a queued lane still reports as waiting.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py`
- `changelog.d/basicly-k6tpep.6.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `30000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: render a board whose only worktrees are parked and read one sentence that names the ready count, with the banner agreeing.

payload.description:
## Context

Four records filed in one session on 2026-08-22 declared a scope naming the wrong module, and all four failed the same way: **the scope was written from where the wrong value renders, not from where it is produced.**

| record | declared | the value is produced in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `basicly-fi1i7z` | `loop.py`, `supervise.py`, `verify.py` | `checkout.py`, `commit.py`, `merge.py` |
| `basicly-eaw1dy` | `board_wall.py` | `board_regions.py` |
| `basicly-0hxck3` | two skill surfaces | skills project to **three** |
| `basicly-a68ggd` | `board_render.py` | `board_regions.py` |

## The cost, and which instrument caught each

`basicly-fi1i7z` reached the landing gate and was routed to rework for changing eleven files outside its declared four. Its work was correct and verified green; the record was wrong. Re-dispatching would have spent about thirty million tokens rebuilding it, and it was recovered only by correcting the record by hand.

`basicly-0hxck3` was caught by `projection-skills` refusing the commit: skills project to `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`, and only one was written.

`basicly-eaw1dy` and `basicly-a68ggd` were caught by probing before dispatch, which cost one command each.

So three of four were caught downstream of the filing, and only the probe was cheap.

## Why the guidance did not prevent it

`decompose-plan` already carries **Declare the scope honestly even though it costs you**, and it is about *size* - a scope declared honestly reads as a bigger lane, so declare it anyway. It says nothing about how to **find** the right files. The failure here is not under-declaring a known set; it is naming a confidently wrong one.

## What was added

A section, **Locate the producer, never the surface**, carrying the four instances, the one-command probe (`rg` for the literal the defect prints, or for the function whose result is wrong), and the follow-up question that catches the projection case: does this value reach more than one surface. A projected artifact usually has several, and a renderer almost always sits one call above the builder that owns the fact.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n -i 'scope' .basicly/core/skills/decompose-plan/skill.yaml`
2. Read every hit and look for any instruction on how to determine which files a fix touches.

**Observed before the change.** Seven hits, all about overlap, serialization and honest sizing. None about locating the producer.

**Control.** The same probe returns seven hits rather than zero, so the file was reached and the absence is real rather than a bad pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an author writes a scope, THE GUIDANCE SHALL give a probe that finds the module producing the wrong value, and the probe SHALL be a command rather than an instruction to think harder.
- WHEN a value reaches more than one surface, THE GUIDANCE SHALL say so, because the projection case is the one a single-file probe misses.
- WHEN the guidance is changed, EVERY PROJECTED ROOT SHALL be rebuilt, which is itself one of the four instances.
- WHERE the existing honest-sizing section stands, IT SHALL NOT be replaced; the two answer different questions.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/decompose-plan/skill.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/decompose-plan/SKILL.md`
- `.agents/skills/decompose-plan/SKILL.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `50000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Read the shipped skill on both projected roots and check the probe is a runnable command, then run that probe against one of the four recorded instances and confirm it names the module the fix actually touched.

payload.description:
## Context

The first `basicly release` since the release-notes gate landed (basicly-7phc, 2026-08-20) refused its own release commit on 2026-08-28: `FAILED: release-notes` in `pre-commit-script`, 32/33 checks passed, and the tree was restored. Measured with `release.accounted_records` logic re-run without the filename source: 43 closed records with a shipped scope would owe a note after assembly, and every one of them has a fragment named for it whose body never cites its own id in parentheses.

`release.accounted_records` counts a record from three sources: the fragment filename, a parenthetical citation in a fragment body, and a parenthetical citation in `CHANGELOG.md`. Its docstring says `CHANGELOG.md` holds both once assembly has deleted the files. It does not: `release._fragment_body` copies the body verbatim, so a fragment that cited its record by filename alone loses its accounting in the very commit that publishes it. The gate and the assembler disagree about what an assembled note carries, and the release is the only commit where that disagreement is visible.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a clean main with 149 fragments, `uv run basicly release 0.10.0 --issue basicly-3mr2zg`.
2. Observe `release failed and the tree was restored: ... FAILED: release-notes`.
3. Control: `uv run python .scripts/check_release_notes.py` on the same tree before the release passes, because the filenames still exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `_assemble_fragments` folds a fragment whose body does not cite its own record id parenthetically, IT SHALL append the citation `(<record-id>)` to the fragment's last non-empty line, so the assembled `CHANGELOG.md` accounts for the record exactly as the filename did.
- WHEN a fragment body already cites its own id parenthetically, IT SHALL be copied unchanged, so the section stays byte-identical for every fragment written correctly.
- WHEN `check_release_notes.py` runs on a tree where a fragment named for a closed record has been assembled by the fixed code, IT SHALL report the record as noted, not owed.
- WHEN the regression test runs, IT SHALL assemble one fragment without a self-citation and one with, and assert the first gains `(<id>)` and the second is unchanged, then assert `accounted_records` over the assembled changelog contains both ids with the fragment files deleted.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/release.py`
- `tests/test_release.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_release.py -q -k assembl` green, then `uv run basicly release 0.10.0 --issue basicly-3mr2zg --dry-run` and the real release commit passing `pre-commit-script`.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Steps to Reproduce

Two processes mint or consume confirm codes concurrently; src/basicly/policy.py:1251-1273 reads the store, modifies it in memory and writes it back with no lock or atomic replace, so one writer's update is lost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two concurrent writers to the confirm-code store when both complete then both writes are present in the store
- Given a reader racing a writer when the store is read then it parses as valid JSON (no torn write is observable)

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`

File one follow-up record against src/basicly/policy.py:1269-1281 with two arms: (1) add a committed subprocess-based regression test for the cross-process arm, so the word 'processes' is bound by a gate rather than by an ad-hoc command, and assert the no-lock control loses a key for the lost-update reason rather than on the pid-keyed tmp collision; (2) decide the 5s crash budget deliberately -- either raise _CONFIRM_HOLD_BUDGET_S with the reasoning recorded, or keep it and add the bound to the next release's entry for this fix. unsupported.claim: Concurrent confirm-code mints and consumes no longer lose each other's writes ... so two checkpoint approvals racing each other keep both codes.
unsupported.why: Looked for a test or gate making the no-loss outcome unconditional and found none; found a counterexample instead. _CONFIRM_HOLD_BUDGET_S = 5.0 at src/basicly/policy.py:1270 means base_lock.hold_file declares a holder older than 5s crashed and steals the lock (src/basicly/base_lock.py:222, 'if age > hold_budget_s and _steal(path)'), after which two writers are inside the guarded region at once and a write is lost with no error. Probe: two processes minting distinct keys, the first sleeping 7s inside its guarded read, leaves keys: ['slow:ship'] -- the second writer's entry is gone. The serialisation claim survives; the unconditional no-loss outcome holds only for a hold that completes inside the 5s crash budget, and the note states no such bound. Separately, no committed test spawns a process, so the word 'processes' is bound only by the ad-hoc command above: tests/test_policy_confirm_store.py::test_concurrent_confirm_code_writers_both_land uses two threads and, with the lock stubbed out, fails on a pid-keyed tmp-file collision (FileNotFoundError on checkpoint-confirms.<pid>.json.tmp) rather than on the lost update the acceptance criteria describe.

payload.description:
## Context
When several sessions claim records on one machine under CPU load, I want every claim to settle (exit 0 or 3), so that a session never ends with an unsettled claim during the vault cutover.

## Finding
tests/test_claim_load.py::test_a_small_real_load_makes_claims_in_every_session_and_one_holder_per_record failed twice in quality-gates run 44526420542 (shard 9/12 and its rerun) on lane harness/ci-weights 6863aeff: assert {0, 3, 4} <= {0, 3}. Exit 4 is UNSETTLED in .basicly/core/kit/tracker/vault_claim.py. The run used pytest --dist worksteal, which ran this 4-session, 2-machine load beside other heavy tests on a 4-vCPU runner. Without worksteal the test passed in 4 earlier runs. Reading (assumed): under CPU contention a claim does not settle in its deadline. The test assertion stays as it is; worksteal was reverted in the lane.

## Links
Related: basicly-eg2w0gg (pending view lock waits over 5 s under eight sessions), basicly-gtb19bg.43.16 (settle, wait for, cancel or expire an unsettled claim), workspace dev-dqsc6 (development cutover after 0.46.5).
payload.title: A claim ends unsettled with exit 4 when sessions claim under CPU load

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: When four sessions on two machines claim records while the other CPUs of a 4-vCPU runner are busy, every claim session ends 0 or 3 and none ends 4 (UNSETTLED).

payload.text: [investigation 2026-11-19 basicly session, evidence so far, n=1 per arm] Reading: the load harness, not the claim deadline, makes claims unsettled under CPU load. .scripts/claim_load.py _claim passes --deadline CLAIM_DEADLINE_S / scale (30 / 8 = 3.75 s real), and its git shim scales push and fetch latency by 1/scale, but CPU work (CLI start, folds, share retries) is not scaled, so at scale 8 CPU contention weighs 8 times more against the budget than in real use. Runs on 4 pinned cores (taskset -c 28-31), config sessions=4 machines=2 minutes=8 seed=3: (1) scale 8, quiet: exits {0:6, 3:2}, claim_s mean 6.41 max 8.33 scaled. (2) scale 8, 4 CPU burners on the same cores: exits {0:6, 3:1, 4:1}; the unsettled claim said "the vault refused the share 2 times; 1 events stay queued; run sync again" after claim_s 3.664 s real of 3.75; claim_s mean 18.09 max 29.31 scaled, joined_wait p99 22.6. (3) scale 1, same 4 burners (real 30 s deadline): exits {0:6, 3:2}, claim_s max 3.53 s real. Not yet shown: the failure rate over repeats, and whether a production claim under heavier contention than 4 burners on 4 cores can still exceed 30 s. Test assertion unchanged.

[investigation 2026-11-19 16:18 UTC, repeats] Setup, runs, claims, exit 4, slowest claim as % of budget: scale 8 + 4 burners 6, 48, 1, 73-98%; scale 8 quiet 5, 40, 0, 28%; scale 1 + 4 burners 6, 48, 0, about 12%; scale 1 + 16 burners on 4 cores 5, 40, 0, 18-21%. Scale 1 never ended unsettled. Cause: the harness divides the whole deadline by scale but scales only the git latency. Option (a) diff sent to the Orchestrator for the owner: CPU_ALLOWANCE_S = 5.0, deadline = CLAIM_DEADLINE_S / scale + CPU_ALLOWANCE_S * (1 - 1 / scale).

payload.description:
When an upgrade re-pins a consumer's CI workflow, I want the previous copy left beside it, so I can see what changed on a file my own rules put on a confirmation list.

Found by the terminal canary and filed there as term-42xuc arm 2. _write_scaffold at cli.py:1219-1241 inverts the safety: the plain path re-pins and writes in place with no backup, while the --overwrite-scaffolds branch writes a .basicly-bak sibling before replacing. So the flag that sounds destructive preserves the original and the default does not.

It is not theoretical for the canary. That repository carries the workflow with five pinned references and holds CI edits on an explicit confirmation list, so an upgrade rewrites a gated file before a human could be asked, and there is no install --dry-run to preview it.

Arm 1 of term-42xuc - a plain install CREATING a workflow where none existed, at the fallthrough that never consults force - is a larger question about what install may do unasked and is filed separately rather than rushed into this patch.
payload.requirements: one branch in _write_scaffold, no new flag and no change to what the force path does. The message names the backup by the same shape the force path already prints, so a consumer meets one vocabulary.
payload.title: back up a scaffold before the default path rewrites it
